On repeated follow‑up testing over 5 years the deficits remained largely stable, with substantial further decline only at a visit in 2020. Since 2015 she developed increasing acoustic, optic, and tactile hallucinations; delusional parasitosis led to self‑wounding scratching behavior.

IBZM‑SPECT (123I‑iodobenzamide, 2015), amyloid‑PET (18F‑florbetaben, 2016), DaT scan (123I‑FP‑CIT, 2015), and 18F‑FDG‑PET (2019) were performed and yielded normal results. She underwent thoracic laminectomy in 2016. Limb weakness continued to worsen over the next years and walking became increasingly restricted.

Neurologic examination showed pseudobulbar palsy; distal muscle weakness without fasciculations but with slightly increased tone; and clearly increased tendon reflexes including bilateral positive Babinski signs, more pronounced in the lower than upper limbs. Electromyography of muscles of all four limbs did not show any indication of active denervation (no fibrillations or positive sharp waves), but showed signs of mild chronic denervation with increased motor unit potential amplitudes and reduced recruitment. Neurographies revealed a pure axonal motor neuropathy of the right peroneal and tibial nerve and a small reduction of amplitudes of the right sural nerve; no signs of demyelination were found. Transcranial magnetic stimulation showed a prolonged central conduction time to the left leg. Sonography of the tongue did not show fasciculations.

Extensive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis did not show indication of inflammatory or paraneoplastic disorder, and neuronal destruction markers including beta‑amyloid, tau, and phosphotau were within normal range. Neurofilament heavy chain in CSF was significantly elevated (NfH 1137 pg/mL), supporting a diagnosis of motoneuron disease. There were no sensory symptoms.
